title: The engagement ring was too big
author: Storytime
hook: My boyfriend proposed at my birthday dinner. The ring was way too big. Then I recognized it.
story: My boyfriend Chris and I have been together for three years. Last Saturday, for my birthday, he took me to the restaurant where we had our first date. Halfway through dessert, he got down on one knee. Everyone in the restaurant turned around. I was crying before he even opened the box. Then he opened it. A gorgeous oval diamond. He slid it on my finger, and it slid right off again. Two sizes too big. Everyone laughed. I laughed. But something about it bothered me. That night, I couldn't sleep. I kept staring at it. And then I remembered where I'd seen it. On Instagram. On his ex, Megan. Five years ago. They were engaged for a year before she called it off. I found her old post. Same oval diamond. Same thin gold band. Same tiny sapphire on the side. He didn't buy me a ring. He gave me hers. When I asked him, he didn't even deny it. He said, it's a perfectly good ring, she gave it back, why waste eleven thousand dollars? I said yes to him. I'm saying no to the ring. Now he says I'm being ungrateful. Am I wrong?
caption: it was a perfectly good ring. for HER 💍 #storytime
sound: a romantic piano that turns suspicious at very low volume
why: Engagement ring drama sparks huge debates, the ring being too big is the planted clue, and the am I wrong ending splits viewers on money versus feelings.

title: The GPS had one saved address
author: Storytime
hook: I bought a used car. The GPS had only one saved address, labeled home. So I drove there.
story: Last month I bought a used car from a dealership. Older model, low miles, great price. The first night, I was messing with the GPS and found one saved address. It just said, home. I was curious, so I hit go. The route took me across town, down streets I knew, onto my street, and stopped right in front of my house. My house. I sat in the driveway with my heart pounding. I hadn't saved anything. The dealer swore the car was wiped. A week later, an old man knocked on my door. He was holding a photo of my house, from the nineteen seventies. He said his name was Walter, and he had lived here for forty years. He raised his kids here. After his wife passed, his family moved him into assisted living and sold his car. My car. He said he used to drive past every Sunday, just to see the house. Then his license got taken away, and he couldn't anymore. He asked if he could see the backyard one more time. His wife had planted the apple tree out back. The one I almost cut down last spring. I let him in. Part two?
caption: the car knew where home was 🏡 #storytime
sound: an eerie, slow music box that turns warm at very low volume
why: Creepy storytime is trending, the saved address is a chilling hook, the twist turns it wholesome, and the apple tree sets up an emotional part two.

title: She asked me to switch my plane seat
author: Storytime
hook: A woman on my flight asked me to switch seats so she could sit next to her husband. I said no. Her husband thanked me.
story: I fly a lot for work, and I always pay extra for an aisle seat. Last week, on an eight hour flight to New York, a woman stopped at my row. She said, hi, could you swap with me? My husband is in the window seat next to you. My seat is in the back row, in the middle, next to the toilets. I felt bad. But I'd paid for this seat. I was about to say yes anyway, when the man by the window caught my eye and very slowly shook his head. So I said, sorry, I'd rather keep my seat. She huffed and walked to the back. For the first hour, the man said nothing. Then, during the meal, he leaned over and said, thank you. I booked separate seats on purpose. I'm flying to New York to sign the divorce papers tomorrow. She thinks we're going on holiday. I nearly choked on my pasta. He said he'd tried to tell her four times. She kept changing the subject. So his lawyer told him to do it in person. At the end of the flight, she came back to collect him, and she was smiling. She has no idea. Should I have switched seats?
caption: he shook his head very slowly ✈️ #storytime
sound: a calm airport lounge beat with a tense note at very low volume
why: Holiday travel season is starting, seat swap requests are a hot debate topic, the husband shaking his head is the planted clue, and the question gets people arguing.
